chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from Muhammad ibn Ali, from Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad Al-Sayrafi, from Ismail ibn Abdul Khaliq, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
Washing the head with the hibiscus is an advertisement (of beauty).

key_terms.بِالْخِطْمِيِّ: With the hibiscus (a plant used for dyeing/grooming)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on washing the head with hibiscus in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from al-Kafi establishes the permissibility and merit of using the hibiscus plant (khittim) for washing the head, linking the physical act to the concept of 'nushrah' (displaying beauty or grooming). In Shia jurisprudence, this highlights the emphasis on cleanliness (taharah) not merely as a ritual requirement but as an act that enhances one's appearance and dignity, reflecting the Prophet's tradition of caring for personal hygiene. The brevity of the narration underscores its status as a well-known practice among the Imams' companions, requiring no further elaboration.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Abu Abdullah, from Muhammad Bin Ali, from Al Hassan Bin Muhammad Al Sayrafi, from Ismail Bin Abdul Khaliq, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Washing the head with the hibiscus is an advertisement (of beauty)’.
en.sarwar: 5. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn abu ‘Abd Allah from Muhammad ibn Ali from al-Hassan ibn Muhammad al- Sayrafiy from ’Isma‘il ibn ‘Abd al-Khaliq who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Washing the head with marshmallow plant is a protective charm.’”
